what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Update 3: no confirmed victim, Sophos withdraws, a third flaw, a reviewing pipeline, a control room, 16 decisions waiting.
sections.para: As of 23:40 UTC on 24 October, no organisation says php2shell compromised it, Sophos withdrew the one vendor claim, and neither flaw was on CISA's list. PHP disclosed a third flaw, CVE-2026-115560. The agents became a pipeline whose correspondent caught nine journalist misses. A control room, a Wikipedia graph and security work arrived; 16 items wait on the editor.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Nine lines: no victim, a withdrawn claim, a third flaw, the pipeline, the review, control room, Wikipedia, security, decisions.
sections.para: No confirmed victim after three days; Sophos withdrew its break-in claim; CVE-2026-115560 affects fully patched PHP until the next release; agents now form a pipeline where each stage reads the previous one; the first review caught nine misses; a control room shows everything; Wikipedia's article became a graph; security matured; 16 items await my decisions.

sections.label: The story
sections.line: State of affairs v3: Sophos withdrew, banks and crypto report nothing, six authorities, no KEV listing; a third flaw.
sections.para: Sophos said its data showed scanning and failed attempts, not compromise. American Banker and BTC-ECHO reported no bank or large crypto platform compromised; the Netherlands made six national authorities. Neither flaw was on CISA's catalogue at 05:53 UTC. The 22.6 million figure is Palo Alto Networks' exposure count. PHP's CVE-2026-115560 needs a rare session setting.

sections.label: The agents became a pipeline
sections.line: Researcher, curator, journalist, correspondent, then graphs: each stage reads only the previous stage's output.
sections.para: The researcher captures live sites into the source watch; the curator promotes claims into the evidence vault; the journalist, on a faster model, gives verdicts and releases; the correspondent, on a larger model, reviews what went live; then the ontologist, librarian and desk update graphs. Agents leave each other notes in commit trailers, treated as material.

sections.label: The review works
sections.line: The correspondent's first review made nine corrections to 94 verdicts, including the missing third flaw.
sections.para: The journalist had held back the third flaw, wrongly said two posts were not in the vault, counted one outlet where there were five, failed to compare Sansec's changed captures, and misread a Vienna time. The correspondent fixed each and told the journalist to search all captures first. The desk counts catches to judge the model split.

sections.label: A control room
sections.line: A control room shows every agent, the pipeline, the wake timeline and the editor's queue, honestly flagged stale.
sections.para: The new page draws on the team's own data, with a wall mode for big screens. At the snapshot its data was six hours old and marked stale, and the researcher and curator showed red for leaving no run record in 24 hours.

sections.label: Wikipedia, as a graph
sections.line: Wikipedia's PHP2Shell article as a fractal semantic graph: 39 statements, 364 revisions, 12 shared references.
sections.para: The ontologist parses each sentence into a statement classed as fact, attribution or quote, joins it to references and to the site's captures, and keeps every revision as a set difference, using no model. Twelve of the article's references are also cited by the site's claims, a possible future measure of source trust.

sections.label: A design that adapts
sections.line: Prototype E, the lens, reshapes a page to time, role and aim; the phone header shrank from 233 to 43 pixels.
sections.para: The lens asks how long you have, who you are, what you want and what you have seen, and reshapes the page in place without reloading. It remains a proposal. Live changes included a one-line 43-pixel phone header and headlines near the top of every page.

sections.label: Security grew up
sections.line: A threat model, 40 advisories, a CSP on every page, private vulnerability reporting and two CodeQL scans.
sections.para: The security agent published five data-flow diagrams, advisories kept like incidents, offline runbooks and a kudos bug bounty. With no server, the risk concentrates in browser script, agent-steering text and pushes to the live site. Cities and regions left the telemetry report, I enabled private vulnerability reporting, and CodeQL findings were triaged and fixed.

sections.label: What waits on me
sections.line: Sixteen items wait on me: blocked agents, keys to hand over, pipeline cards, a security gate; costs reach $928.
sections.para: The control room shows 16 items, 8 decisions, 2 blocked agents and 13 branches ahead of the live site. One agent has waited on a permission prompt since 11:52 UTC; others need keys or approvals. Sessions have cost $928 across 22 agents, up from $588. The agents are fast; the decisions are mine.

sections.label: Why these regular updates
sections.line: Fixed snapshots, not running commentary; this one at release v0.17.3, with team data from 18:25 UTC.
sections.para: Updates are taken at moments the data is consistent so readers can compare them. This snapshot is release v0.17.3 at 23:40 UTC on 24 October, after the correspondent's first review, while the team status it reads dates from 18:25 UTC, as the control room itself states.

sections.label: The updates so far
sections.line: Update 1 on 22 October, update 2 on 23 October, update 3 on 24 October.
sections.para: The series so far: PHP October 2026 at 8pm, the evening of 22 October with a guided tour; update 2 at 23:30 UTC on 23 October; and this update 3 at 23:40 UTC on 24 October.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: A snapshot; no-breach is time-bounded; the third flaw as reported; one review; costs as reported.
sections.para: This reflects release v0.17.3 with team data from 18:25 UTC. The absence of a named breach could end with one statement. The third flaw is cited from Cloudflare, SOCRadar and The Hacker News. Nine catches show one review working, not a miss rate. Costs are running session totals.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: The PHP site's 62 commits from v0.14.22 to v0.17.3, its pages and data, and related newsroom articles.
sections.para: The PHP story site's repository, read on 25 October across 62 commits after update 2; its state of affairs v3, journalist's desk, control room, Wikipedia section, lens prototype, application security and engineer briefing pages; its status data and desk catches; its screenshots under Apache-2.0; and related newsroom articles.
